steps.body: **Expanding** unpacks one log into a sum/difference of simple logs — outside-in: quotient first, then products, then powers. **Condensing** reverses it — coefficients become powers FIRST, then sums merge into products and differences into quotients. Two directions, opposite orders.

options.label: log (x²y)
options.feedback: Right — the 2 climbs up as a power, then the sum multiplies.

options.label: log (2xy)
options.feedback: A coefficient becomes an EXPONENT, not a factor: 2 log x = log (x²).

options.label: log (x² + y)
options.feedback: A SUM of logs condenses to a PRODUCT inside — never a sum inside.

options.label: 2 log (xy)
options.feedback: The 2 belongs to x alone — absorb it before merging: x², then times y.

steps.body: Order matters when condensing: **coefficients become exponents before anything merges**. 3 log₂ x − log₂ y: first 3 log₂ x = log₂ (x³), then the difference divides: **log₂ (x³/y)**. Merging first (log₂(x/y) then cubing everything) would wrongly cube the y too.

explanationVariants: 4 log₃ x − log₃ y: power first (x⁴), then the minus divides: log₃ (x⁴/y).

options.label: log₃ (x⁴y)
options.feedback: The MINUS divides — y lands in the denominator.

options.label: log₃ ((x/y)⁴)
options.feedback: The 4 belongs to x alone — merging first wrongly raises y to the 4th too.

options.label: log₃ (4x/y)
options.feedback: The coefficient 4 becomes the EXPONENT on x, not a factor: x⁴/y.

options.label: 2 log₅ x − 3 log₅ y
options.feedback: Right — quotient splits to a difference; both powers march out.

options.label: 2 log₅ x + 3 log₅ y
options.feedback: y³ is UNDERNEATH — its whole term exits with a minus.

options.label: (2/3) log₅ (x/y)
options.feedback: Each power belongs to its own factor — they exit separately: 2 on x's log, 3 on y's.

options.label: 6 log₅ (x/y)
options.feedback: The exponents 2 and 3 never multiply together — split the quotient first, then move each power.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.

explanationVariants: (log₂ x)/(log₂ y) is a QUOTIENT OF LOGS — no property touches it; log₂(x/y) = log₂ x − log₂ y is different. Witness x = 8, y = 2: difference is 2, quotient is 3.
The quotient property acts on a quotient INSIDE one log.

widget.prompt: Which equals log₂ x − log₂ y?

options.label: log₂ (x/y)
options.feedback: Right — a difference of logs condenses to the log of a quotient.

options.label: (log₂ x)/(log₂ y)
options.feedback: Dividing the LOGS is different — witness x = 8, y = 2: the difference is 3 − 1 = 2, but 3/1 = 3.

options.label: log₂ (x − y)
options.feedback: Differences INSIDE have no rule — witness x = 8, y = 2: log₂ 6 ≈ 2.58 ≠ 2.

options.label: log₂ x · log₂ (1/y)
options.feedback: That's a PRODUCT of logs (3 · (−1) = −3 at the witness) — the true rewrite adds log₂(1/y): subtraction in disguise.

explanationVariants: (1/2) log 16 + 2 log 5: powers first — log (16^(1/2)) + log 25 = log 4 + log 25 = log 100 = 2.
Half-power is a square root: √16 = 4; then 4 · 25 = 100.

numericErrors.feedback: Coefficients become EXPONENTS (√16 = 4, 5² = 25), then multiply: log 100 = 2 — never add the raw numbers.
√16 = 4 — the half-coefficient takes a square ROOT, not half of 16: 4 · 25 = 100, and log 100 = 2.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.

hints: Coefficients up: (1/2) log 16 = log √16 = log 4; 2 log 5 = log 25.

takeaways: When condensing, coefficients become exponents BEFORE any merge.
Quotients of logs and logs of sums have NO rules — witness values expose fakes.
Clean numeric answers often hide inside condensed products.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: change of base, and equations no matching can crack.

concept.body: One condense in slow motion: 2 log 3 = log (3²) = log 9. The coefficient climbed up as an exponent.

commonErrors.feedback: Condense: 2 · 5 = 10 inside — log 10 = 1 (7 adds the raw numbers).
10 is the product INSIDE — its base-10 log is 1.
